Berke followed Islam, and Muslim merchants traveled Volga and steppe routes. Envoys, traders and interpreters could bring distant news while pursuing different business. At court, a visitor's patron and the intended recipient of a letter mattered when assessing a message. Escorts needed destinations, hosts and document handovers. Waiting for an audience consumed food and fodder, and changed routes could separate letters, replies and promises.

At court, a visitor's patron and the intended recipient of a letter mattered when assessing a message. Hosts asked whom visitors represented, what they could authorize and how to return gifts and replies. Kin and interpreters helped, while mistranslation damaged promises and standing.
